---
title: "Mass Balance Calculator"
output: 
  pdf_document: default
  html_notebook: default
---

This notebook has been prepared to enable calculation of the mass balance of the Rolleston glacier.

Snow depth measurements are collected at the end of each winter, as well as a snow density profile.
At the end of summer more snow depth measurements are made, and another snow density profile. In addition, the  total depth of summer melt at four locations is found.
From these observations, together with glacier extent and elevation data the mass balance values are found.

End of winter accumulation interpolation uses universal kriging by default - the depth histograms and sample variogram of the residuals and the data should be visually checked to see if this is appropriate. Similarly, end of summer uses ordinary kriging by default, but the depth histograms and sample variograms need to be checked to confirm this is appropriate.

The mass balance values required (for submission to the World Glacier Monitoring Service) are:
Dates of the beginning of the survey period, the end of winter observation date, and the end-of-survey date.
The equilibrium line elevation and uncertainty
The minimum number of observations in the accumulation area for all surveys undertaken during the year
The maximum number of observations in the ablation area for all surveys undertaken during the year
The size of the accumulation area and uncertainty
The size of the ablation area and uncertainty
Accumulation area ratio
Specific winter balance and uncertainty
Specific summer balance and uncertainty
Specific annual balance and uncertainty
Location and mass balance of each observation (with uncertainty) for all probe and stake locations

The most calculations required are for the:
1/ snow density extrapolation to all depths
2/ The specific mass balances (which requires interpolation of the observations).

Stuff to do:
I need to add another field to the stake data that provides an identifier.
Currently I decide on which stakes are the same by their location, but sometimes the GPS error is enough that I get a mix up

# Define useful functions
```{r}
#See this link to explain what the setAs is all about. I use it to predefine the date format in the StakeData.csv file I load later on. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13022299/specify-custom-date-format-for-colclasses-argument-in-read-table-read-csv
setAs("character","myDate", function(from) as.Date(from, format="%d/%m/%Y") )

#The following is a function to create a depth to average density look-up-table based on some snow pit data.
#Create a table of densities that extrapolates the observed depths down to 20 m  (which is assumed to be a maximum, who is going to probe a 20 m hole?) in 10 cm steps. The densities below the pit depth are taken as the average of the metre above.
#Also calculate the average density for each total depth (i.e. from the surface to the depth).
DepthToDensityLUT <- function(SinglePitData) {
  
  #Get the data of interest
  Densities <- SinglePitData[,c(3:9)]
  
  #Create a vector of depths from 0 to 20 m
  Depths <- seq(from = 0, to = 20000, by = 100)
  
  #For the special case where only a single density observation is taken, all snow densities are the same
  if (nrow(Densities) == 1){
    DepthDensities <- data.frame(Depths=Depths,Density=rep(Densities$Density..kg.m3.,length(Depths)))
  } else {
    #The usual case where several density measurements have been taken to different depths
    DepthDensities <- approx(x=Densities$Depth.to.bottom..mm., 
                             y=Densities$Density..kg.m3., xout = Depths, rule = 2:1)
    
    #Convert to a dataframe
    DepthDensities <- as.data.frame(do.call(cbind, DepthDensities))
    names(DepthDensities) <- c("Depth","Density")
    
    #Extend the densities down to 20 m assuming each 100 mm deeper has a density that is the average of the metre above
    for (Depth in Depths[which(Depths > max(Densities$Depth.to.bottom..mm.))]) {
      #browser()
      DepthDensities[DepthDensities$Depth == Depth,'Density'] <- mean(DepthDensities[(DepthDensities$Depth > (Depth - 1000) & DepthDensities$Depth < Depth),'Density'])
    }
  }
  #Round the density values
  DepthDensities$Density <- round(DepthDensities$Density)
  
  #Calculate the average density from the surface to each depth value
  DepthDensities$AveDensity <- sapply(DepthDensities$Depth, function(x) {mean(DepthDensities$Density[DepthDensities$Depth <= x])})
  return(DepthDensities)
}

#This function takes a snow depth and a date and the list of snow pit density data and calculates the SWE
SnowDepthToSWE <- function(SnowDepth, Date, PitData) {
  #Get the PitData index for the date of interest
  PitDataIndex <- which(sapply(PitData, function(x) x$Date[1] == Date)==TRUE)
  
  #Create the Depth-to-Density look up table from the PitData
  DepthToDensity <- DepthToDensityLUT(PitData[[PitDataIndex]])
  
  #Get the average density for the depth of interest
  AverageDensity <- approx(DepthToDensity$Depth, DepthToDensity$AveDensity, xout = SnowDepth)$y
  SWE <- SnowDepth / 1000 * AverageDensity
}
```

# Define file locations, data sources and constants.
Some files vary with the year, e.g. probe and pit data (but not stake data).
Some data needs to be pre-prepared, e.g. the spatial accumulation/ablation area outlines, density uncertainty and area uncertainty.
Some data only occasionally changes (e.g. glacier outlines).
```{r}
#Set the working directory to the same location as this file
setwd(this.path::this.dir())
ProjectDirectory <- "../"
DataDirectory <- file.path(ProjectDirectory,"data")
GISDirectory <- file.path(ProjectDirectory,"GIS")

IceDensity <- 917 # kilograms per cubic metre, from Patterson 
#****************************************
#Edit the date
#Define the mass balance year. This is the year of the end-of-summer
MassBalanceYear <- 2025

# Standard deviation for density is calculated over all years (currently 2010-2026) based on Cullen et al. (2017) by a separate script (density_standard_dev.R) and hardcoded here
EOW_density_sd_all <- 32 #kg/m3 end of winter
EOS_density_sd_all <- 56.4 # end of summer
# Glacier area/outline uncertainty (Paul et al., 2013)
rel_sigma_area <- 0.036

#Search the data directories for the appropriate data files.
#Currently all stake data are saved to a single file, whereas the probe and density data are saved in their own files for each survey under a directory named for the survey. 
CurrentYearDataDirectory <- file.path(DataDirectory,"IndividualYears",paste0(MassBalanceYear -1,"-",MassBalanceYear))

DepthFileNameList <- list.files(path = CurrentYearDataDirectory, pattern = "Rolleston_depths_.*csv$",full.names=TRUE)
DensityFileNameList <- list.files(path = CurrentYearDataDirectory, pattern = "Rolleston_density_.*csv$",full.names = TRUE)

if (MassBalanceYear < 2022) {
  RollestonGlacierOutlineFile <- "Rolleston_outline_20090408V3.shp"
} else if (MassBalanceYear < 2025){
  RollestonGlacierOutlineFile <- "Rolleston_outline_20220408_Sentinel2_NDSI.shp"
} else {
  RollestonGlacierOutlineFile <- "Rolleston_outline_20250313_Sentinel2_NDSI.shp"
}

StakeFileName       <- file.path(DataDirectory,"Rolleston_Stakes.csv")
RollestonDEMFile <- file.path(GISDirectory,"rolelevnztm")

#Find the filename of the Accumulation Ablation Shapefile. Note that this has to have an attribute called "Type" with the accumulation area polygon called "Accumulation", and the ablation polygon called "Ablation". It should be possible to create this using the glacier outline and the EOSS line. Something for the future.
AccumulationAblationShapefileName <- list.files(file.path(GISDirectory,paste0(MassBalanceYear -1,"-",MassBalanceYear)),pattern = "^AccumulationAblation.*shp$",full.names  = TRUE)

#Find the filename of the end-of-summer-snowline shapefile. Note that this is a lineshape file.
EOSSShapefileName <- list.files(file.path(GISDirectory,paste0(MassBalanceYear -1,"-",MassBalanceYear)),pattern = "^EOSS.*shp$",full.names  = TRUE)
```

# Load the spatial data, static and observed.
 - Glacier outline, 
 - End-Of-Summer snowline line shapefile, 
 - DEM, 
 - Accumulation/Ablation polygon shapefile, 
 - stake points, 
 - pit location and
 - probe locations.
```{r,fig.height=5,fig.width=7.5}
#Load the glacier outline and explicitly set the projection to NZTM
RollestonGlacierOutline <- terra::vect(file.path(GISDirectory,RollestonGlacierOutlineFile)) %>% terra::project(y="epsg:2193")

#Get the DEM data
RollestonDEM <- terra::rast(RollestonDEMFile) %>% 
  terra::project(y="epsg:2193") %>%
  terra::crop(RollestonGlacierOutline)

#Create a spatial point file of 30 m grid spacing across the glacier for use in kriging
GlacierGrid <- st_as_sf(RollestonGlacierOutline) %>% 
  st_buffer(15) %>%
  st_make_grid(cellsize = 30, what = "centers") %>%
  terra::vect() %>%
  terra::project(y="epsg:2193")

#Add a "DEMValues" attribute to the Glacier Grid, so that elevation can be used in the kriging
GlacierGrid$DEMValues <- terra::extract(RollestonDEM, GlacierGrid,ID=FALSE)

#Load the end of summer accumulation and ablation area shape file and explicitly set the projection to NZTM
AccumulationAblationAreas <- terra::vect(AccumulationAblationShapefileName)
# Assign CRS if missing (some older shapefiles lack a .prj file)
if (is.na(terra::crs(AccumulationAblationAreas)) || terra::crs(AccumulationAblationAreas) == "") {
  message("AccumulationAblationAreas has no CRS — assuming NZTM (EPSG:2193)")
  terra::crs(AccumulationAblationAreas) <- "epsg:2193"
} else {
  AccumulationAblationAreas <- terra::project(AccumulationAblationAreas, y = "epsg:2193")
}

#Load the end of summer snow line shape file and explicitly set the projection to NZTM
EOSSLine <- terra::vect(EOSSShapefileName) %>% terra::project(y="epsg:2193")



#Get the data. Note that stake data is for all years, so is in a different directory
PitData   <- lapply(DensityFileNameList, read.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,colClasses = c("character","character","myDate",rep("numeric",6),"character"))

ProbeData <- lapply(DepthFileNameList, read.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,colClasses = c("character","character","character",rep("numeric",4),"character"))

#Clean Probe Data to get rid of > and < signs present in some years
ProbeData <- lapply(ProbeData, function(df) {
  df[4:7] <- lapply(df[4:7], function(x) {
    x <- gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", x)  # strips > < etc
    as.numeric(x)
  })
  df
})

ProbedDates <- as.Date(sub("Rolleston_depths_","",file_path_sans_ext(basename(DepthFileNameList))),format="%Y%m%d")

#Check that only two probing dates are involved. This assumption is required for some of the subsequent analysis.
#If more than 2 probing dates, then some manual calculations are needed.
if (length(unique(ProbedDates))> 2)print("More than two probing dates in a year. Need to manually figure it all out!!")

#Find if depth files are virtual measurements. That is, depths created manually based on expert opinion.
WhichVirtual <- grep("virtual",basename(DepthFileNameList))

#assume that the earlier date is the winter observations, and the later is summer.
#Name the non-virtual data
names(ProbeData) <- NA #Need to provide dummy names before manipulating them individually.

if(length(WhichVirtual) > 0){
  names(ProbeData)[-WhichVirtual][order(ProbedDates[-WhichVirtual])] <- c("EndOfWinter","EndOfSummer")
  
  #Name the virtual data based on it's date
  names(ProbeData)[WhichVirtual] <-
    paste0(names(ProbeData)[match(ProbedDates[WhichVirtual],ProbedDates[-WhichVirtual])] ,"_Virtual")   
} else {
  names(ProbeData)[order(ProbedDates)] <- c("EndOfWinter","EndOfSummer")
}
StakeData <- read.csv(StakeFileName,stringsAsFactors = FALSE,colClasses = c("myDate","character",rep("numeric",5),"character"))
#Limit the stake data to just the date(s) of interest, taken to be any dates before September of the mass balance year, but after the previous September
StakeData <- StakeData[StakeData$Date > as.Date(paste(MassBalanceYear - 1,"09","01"),"%Y %m %d") & 
                         StakeData$Date < as.Date(paste(MassBalanceYear,"09","01"),"%Y %m %d"),]

#Convert the point data to spatial data
spProbePoints <- lapply(ProbeData, function(x) {
  #these data are to be used for Kriging, which cannot have duplicate locations,
  # though having nearby locations is useful for calculating the nugget.
  # So to keep the duplicates, their position is edited by 1 m in any direction
  if(any(duplicated(x[,c("Easting_NZTM","Northing_NZTM")]))){
    NoDuplicateCoordinates <- geoR::jitterDupCoords(x[,c("Easting_NZTM","Northing_NZTM")],max = 1, which.fix = "last")
    #Replace the old coordinates with the new "de-duplicated" coordinates
    x[,c("Easting_NZTM.","Northing_NZTM")] <- NoDuplicateCoordinates
  }
  terra::vect(x, geom=c("Easting_NZTM","Northing_NZTM"), crs="epsg:2193")
  })

spStakePoints <- terra::vect(StakeData, geom=c("E_NZTM","N_NZTM"), crs="epsg:2193")

#Get the extents of the glacier in lat lon
GlacierExtentLatLon <- terra::project(RollestonGlacierOutline, y='epsg:4326') %>% terra::ext()

#Expand the extents to provide extents for the topographical map to download
MapExtents <- GlacierExtentLatLon + 0.005
```

# Hypsometric curve
This chunk takes the DEM and develops an area-elevation hypsometric curve.
```{r}
#Clip the DEM to the Rolleston Glacier area
GlacierDEM <- terra::mask(RollestonDEM,RollestonGlacierOutline)
DEMData <- terra::values(GlacierDEM)
DEMData <- DEMData[!is.na(DEMData)]
DEMData <- DEMData[order(DEMData)]

#From the DEM bin all the elevations into equal sized bins
DEMBins <- split(DEMData, ceiling(seq_along(DEMData)/20))

#Calculate the area in each bin (same as the number of cells multiplied by the resolution) and the average elevation of each bin
BinAreas <- sapply(DEMBins, function(x) {length(x) * prod(terra::res(GlacierDEM))})
BinElevations <- sapply(DEMBins, mean)
BinAreaBelow <- cumsum(BinAreas)

#Build the look up table of elevation vs total area
AreaElevationCurve <- data.frame(Area = BinAreaBelow, Elevation = BinElevations)

#Plot it to have a look
plot(AreaElevationCurve,typ="l")
```

# End of Winter Snow Water Equivalent Interpolation
Calculate the end of winter snow water equivalent by interpolating snow depth measurements (converted to SWE using density observations)  using kriging across the glacier domain. 

Start by:
 - removing duplicates,
 - converting the end of winter snow depths to SWE.
 - getting the elevation for each point, 
 - removing any NA's and 
 - converting the resulting end of winter SWE data to an sf object.
```{r}
#Get the end of winter snow depths
EndOfWinterDepths <- spProbePoints[["EndOfWinter"]]

#remove any duplicate coordinates otherwise the Kriging results in NA's see https://gis.stackexchange.com/questions/250862/r-kriging-cross-validation-returns-na-for-all-prediction-points.
#There shouldn't be any duplicates as duplicates were "jittered" earlier on. Jittering is a better approach than removing duplicates as it retains nearby data that helps determine the variability at small distances, which is needed for the variogram.
EndOfWinterDepths = terra::unique(EndOfWinterDepths)

#Convert to snow water equivalent in mm using the pit data and SWE function
EndOfWinterDepths$SWE <- SnowDepthToSWE(EndOfWinterDepths$Snow_Depth_m*1000, min(ProbedDates),PitData = PitData) 

#Extract elevation from DEM for each probe point
EndOfWinterDepths$DEMValues <- terra::extract(RollestonDEM, EndOfWinterDepths,ID=FALSE)

#Get rid of na values
EndOfWinterDepths <- EndOfWinterDepths[
  !is.na(EndOfWinterDepths$SWE) &
  !is.na(EndOfWinterDepths$DEMValues),
]

#convert EndoFWinterDepths to an sf object to use it in variogram()
eow_depths_sf = sf::st_as_sf(EndOfWinterDepths) 
```


Check whether the data are normally distributed.
Check if there is a trend related to elevation.
This is needed to decide if ordinary or universal kriging should be used.
Ordinary kriging assumes there is no spatial trend, Universal kriging assumes a systematic trend.
Need an objective threshold of how "normal" the distribution needs to be before ordinary kriging is acceptable. Currently assessment is subjective.
Similarly, how "normal" do the residuals from the elevation relationship need to be for Universal kriging to be acceptable.
```{r}
#Check for skew
hist(EndOfWinterDepths$SWE)

# check if there is a trend in SWE with elevation
plot(eow_depths_sf$DEMValues, eow_depths_sf$SWE,
     xlab = "Elevation (m)",
     ylab = "SWE (mm)")
abline(lm(SWE ~ DEMValues, data = eow_depths_sf))

#fit a trend model, plot the histogram of the residuals
elev_mod <- lm(SWE ~ DEMValues, data = eow_depths_sf)
eow_depths_sf$resid <- residuals(elev_mod)
hist(eow_depths_sf$resid)
```

Check whether there is any directional trend (i.e. anisotropy).
This is currently ignored as the later kriging does not (yet) consider anisotropy
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Check for anisotropy - plot the semivariogram in four dirctions and see if it changes
anis_test <- variogram(SWE ~ 1,eow_depths_sf, cutoff=200, alpha = 80,tol.hor = 20)
plot(anis_test)
```

Plot variograms with and without considering the elevation trend.
If they are subjectively the same then, consider ordinary kriging.
The lower the semivariance the better, so if one plots lower than the other, it is the one to use.
Usually kriging the residuals will have lower semivariance, but maybe not always...
```{r}
#Cutoff heuristic - get coordinates, calculate max distance between any two points for variogram cutoff based on https://rpubs.com/Dr_Gurpreet/spatial_interpolation_kriging_R
coords <- terra::crds(EndOfWinterDepths)
dists <- dist(coords)
max_dist <- max(dists)
cutoff <- max_dist / 2

#generate experimental/sample variogram from residuals after removing elevation trend. 
SampleVariogram <- variogram(SWE ~ DEMValues,eow_depths_sf, cutoff = cutoff) 

#compare residual variogram to variogram plotted from the data 
SampleVariogram_ordinary <- variogram(SWE ~ 1, eow_depths_sf, cutoff = cutoff,alpha = 80,tol.hor = 20)

#Plot on one graph
# Set axis limits
xlim <- range(c(SampleVariogram$dist,SampleVariogram_ordinary$dist))
ylim <- range(c(SampleVariogram$gamma,SampleVariogram_ordinary$gamma))

# Create plot
plot(SampleVariogram$dist,
     SampleVariogram$gamma,
     col = "blue",
     xlim = xlim,
     ylim = ylim,
     xlab = "Distance",
     ylab = "Semivariance",
     main="Sample Variograms EOW")

# Add second variogram
points(SampleVariogram_ordinary$dist,
       SampleVariogram_ordinary$gamma,
       col = "red")

legend("topleft",
       legend = c("Residuals", "Ordinary"),
       col = c("blue", "red"),
       pch = c(1, 1))
```

Test variogram models - currently only testing spherical, gaussian and exponential.

Universal kriging is then applied using best the fit model.
This needs editing if Ordinary kriging directly on SWE values are to be used, based on previous tests that might show the data are normally distributed and the semi-variogram is no worse than the residuals one.
```{r}
#see examples of vgm models:
#show.vgms()

#choosing start sill, nugget and range values. these work because fit.variogram() optimises these and needs a reasonable starting point. check that these look realistic on plotted sample variogram
nugget.start <- SampleVariogram$gamma[1]
total.sill <- max(SampleVariogram$gamma)
psill.start <- total.sill - nugget.start
range.start <- max(SampleVariogram$dist)/2

#fitting different models to compare. gaussian unlikely to be any good?
#fit.variogram only optimises sill/range/nugget, anisotropy values are fixed.
sph.fit <- fit.variogram(
  SampleVariogram,
  vgm(psill=psill.start, "Sph", range=range.start, nugget=nugget.start),
  fit.method=7
)

exp.fit <- fit.variogram(
  SampleVariogram,
  vgm(psill=psill.start, "Exp", range=range.start, nugget=nugget.start),
  fit.method=7
)

gau.fit <- fit.variogram(
  SampleVariogram,
  vgm(psill=psill.start, "Gau", range=range.start, nugget=nugget.start),
  fit.method=7
)

#plot to visually compare - check that whichever model is automatically selected looks reasonable
plot(SampleVariogram, sph.fit, main="sph")
plot(SampleVariogram, exp.fit, main="exp")
plot(SampleVariogram, gau.fit, main="gau")

# Collect the SSErr values, pick the best model (lowest weighted residual sum of squares)
sserr <- c(Sph=attr(sph.fit, "SSErr"), Exp=attr(exp.fit, "SSErr"), Gau=attr(gau.fit, "SSErr"))
best_model_name <- names(which.min(sserr))
message("Auto-selected model: ", best_model_name)
vari.model <- list(Sph=sph.fit, Exp=exp.fit, Gau=gau.fit)[[best_model_name]]

#Universal kriging. Using 12 points at a time. Spatial data needs to be an sf object. 
#Point kriging onto the grid, predicts SWE and variance at each cell
KrigedSWE <- krige(SWE~DEMValues,locations=eow_depths_sf,newdata=sf::st_as_sf(GlacierGrid),model=vari.model, nmax=12)

#Ordinary kriging - uncomment the following line
#KrigedSWE <- krige(SWE~1,locations=eow_depths_sf,newdata=sf::st_as_sf(GlacierGrid),model=vari.model, nmax=12)

```

Assess kriging results using leave one out cross validation: each observation is removed, predicted using the remaining data, and compared to the observed value
This tells us how well the kriging predictions match reality at sampled locations.
```{r}
#leave out out cross validation (cv)
cv <- krige.cv(SWE~DEMValues,locations=eow_depths_sf,model=vari.model,nmax=12,debug.level=0)

#plot cv results. dashed line is 1:1 line
cv_df <- data.frame(
  observed = cv$observed,
  predicted = cv$var1.pred
)
ggplot(cv_df, aes(x = observed, y = predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_equal() +
  xlab("Observed SWE (mm w.e.)") +
  ylab("Predicted SWE (mm w.e.)")+ggtitle("Cross validation results EOW")
```

Uncertainty calculations
It is assumed that depth errors from probing are captured by the variogram nugget and have no bias.
I haven't considered errors from the glacier outline, EOSS line, GPS error
```{r}
# error calculations from leave one out cross validation results
ME <- mean(cv$residual) # Bias
RMSE <- sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2)) # Overall prediction error magnitude.
MSDR <- mean((cv$residual^2) / cv$var1.var) # If ~1, kriging variance is a reliable measure of uncertainty, if >1, kriging is underestimating, if <1, kriging is overestimating uncertainty

paste0("Mean error: ", sprintf("%.2f", ME), " (mm w.e.)") 
paste0("Root mean squared error: ", sprintf("%.2f", RMSE), " (mm w.e.)") 
paste0("Mean squared deviation ratio: ", sprintf("%.2f", MSDR))

# Kriging variance raster (rasterise, resample to 5m, crop to glacier extent)
EOWSWEVarRaster <- terra::rasterize(KrigedSWE_v, r, field = 'var1.var')
EOWSWEVarRaster5m <- terra::resample(EOWSWEVarRaster, RollestonDEM)
EOWSWEVarRaster5mGlacier <- terra::mask(EOWSWEVarRaster5m, RollestonGlacierOutline)

# Convert prediction variance (mm2 w.e.) to kriging standard deviation (mm w.e., same as SWE)
EOWSWESERaster5mGlacier <- sqrt(EOWSWEVarRaster5mGlacier)

# Plot kriging error for EOW SWE with probe locations
{
plot(EOWSWESERaster5mGlacier,
     main = "EOW Kriging Standard Deviation (mm w.e.)",
     col = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
     legend = TRUE)
plot(RollestonGlacierOutline, add = T)
plot(EndOfWinterDepths, add=T)
}

# Root mean square (RMS) kriging standard error over the glacier. 
# This summarises the average pixel-scale interpolation uncertainty
sigma_EOW_krig    <- sqrt(mean(EOWSWEVarRaster5mGlacier[], na.rm = TRUE))

# Uncertainty from assumption of uniform density profile
# Get EOW pit by filtering on survey month, then get the LUT and extract average density at maximum pit depth. 
EOWPitData <- PitData[[which(sapply(PitData, function(x) {
  as.integer(format(as.Date(x[1, 3], format = "%d/%m/%Y"), "%m")) %in% 10:12 # October to December for EOW pit
}))]]
EOWPitLUT  <- DepthToDensityLUT(EOWPitData)
EOWMaxDepth <- max(EOWPitData[, 8], na.rm = TRUE)   # column 8 is depth to bottom
EOW_density_mean <- EOWPitLUT$AveDensity[EOWPitLUT$Depth == EOWMaxDepth]

# Pixel-level uncertainty (mm we)
sigma_bw_density_raster <- (EOWSWERaster5mGlacier / EOW_density_mean) * EOW_density_sd_all
sigma_bw_combined <- sqrt(EOWSWEVarRaster5mGlacier + sigma_bw_density_raster^2)

# Glacier-wide combined uncertainty 
sigma_Bw_density <- sqrt(mean(sigma_bw_density_raster[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))
sigma_Bw_total <- sqrt(mean(sigma_bw_combined[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))

paste0("σ kriging: ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_EOW_krig), " mm w.e.")
paste0("σ density: ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bw_density), " mm w.e.")
paste0("σ total (combined): ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bw_total), " mm w.e.")

# Uncertainty contributions
var_krig    <- mean(EOWSWEVarRaster5mGlacier[],      na.rm = TRUE)
var_density <- mean(sigma_bw_density_raster[]^2,     na.rm = TRUE)
total_var   <- var_krig + var_density

paste0(sprintf("Kriging uncertainty contribution:  %.1f%%", 100 * var_krig    / total_var))
paste0(sprintf("Density uncertainty contribution:  %.1f%%", 100 * var_density / total_var))
```

# End of summer (EOS) ablation area interpolation
Figure out the total snow and ice melt depth for each stake location.
This requires working through each of the stakes from the survey start time, and finding the stake from the later survey that is nearest it and how much has emerged.
Also need to look for any intermediate re-drilling of stakes, and account for that as well (e.g. 20th December 2016, 17th January 2018, 13th December 2020)
```{r}
#Get all the survey dates
SurveyDates <- unique(StakeData$Date)

#If there are more than two survey dates, then the stakes were probably reset part way through
#the summer.
#If it is reset, then there should be two rows in the stake data for each stake on the date of the reset.
#One entry gives the length of stake sticking out before re-drilling, the other entry is how much is sticking out after the re-drilling
#The melt calculations assume that the measurement with the most stake sticking out is the pre-drill measurement, but that is not necessarily so.
#It could be possible that a stake put in a re-drilled hole could have a lot of stake sticking out, especially if an extra length of stake had been attached. This should be double checked manually.
#A message is printed recommending to check that the entry with the most stake sticking out really is the pre-drilled measurement. 
if (length(SurveyDates) > 2){
        #Assume stake resetting occured on survey dates that were not the first or the last. 
        StakeResetDates <- SurveyDates[-c(1,length(SurveyDates))]
        print(paste("Double check manually that for the stake reset measurements on ",StakeResetDates, 
                 "that the measurements with the most emerged stake were all before the stake hole was re-drilled.",
                 "Otherwise the total melt calculations will be wrong and should be done manually."))
        print("2016-12-20, 2018-01-17 and 2020-12-13 are all OK")
      #knitr::kable(StakeData[StakeData$Date %in% StakeResetDates,])
}

FirstStakeIndices <- which(StakeData$Date == min(SurveyDates))

#Initialise TotalSurfaceLowering, and TotalSWEMelt vectors
TotalSurfaceLowering <- rep(0,length(FirstStakeIndices))
TotalSWEMelt <- rep(0,length(FirstStakeIndices))

#loop through each stake
for (StakeIndex in FirstStakeIndices){
  StakeOfInterest <- StakeData[StakeIndex,]
  InitialSnowDepth <- StakeOfInterest$Snow_Depth_m
  StakeEmergence <- StakeOfInterest$length_of_stake_emerged_mm
  #Check if other stake data exist within 20 m, assumed to be the same stake
  #This uses the nn2 function which finds the indices of points within a certain radius
  SameStakeIndices <- which(nn2(StakeData[StakeIndex,c(4,5)],StakeData[,c(4,5)],radius = 20, searchtype = "radius")$nn.idx ==1)
  #Get dates of surveys of this stake
  ThisStakesSurveyDates <- unique(StakeData$Date[SameStakeIndices])
  
  #Check that a final survey date exists. If it doesn't then the stake was lost.
  
  
  #now loop through each of these dates, gathering information as you go
  for (SurveyDate in ThisStakesSurveyDates[-1]) {

    #Determine if the survey is a reset, or the last survey for the stake.

    NextSurveyIndices <- SameStakeIndices[which(StakeData$Date[SameStakeIndices] == SurveyDate)]
   # if(length(NextSurveyIndices) > InitialSnowDepth) {
    if(length(NextSurveyIndices) > 1) {
      
      TotalSurfaceLowering[StakeIndex] <- max(StakeData$length_of_stake_emerged_mm[NextSurveyIndices]) - 
        StakeEmergence + 
        TotalSurfaceLowering[StakeIndex]
      StakeEmergence <- min(StakeData$length_of_stake_emerged_mm[NextSurveyIndices]) 
    } else {
      #browser()
      TotalSurfaceLowering[StakeIndex] <- StakeData$length_of_stake_emerged_mm[NextSurveyIndices] - 
        StakeEmergence + 
        TotalSurfaceLowering[StakeIndex]
      FinalSnowDepth <- StakeData$Snow_Depth_m[NextSurveyIndices]
      }
  }
  #Stake melt may sometimes be just snow, or a mix of snow and ice.
      #If the total surface lowering is greater than the initial snow depth, then the total snow melt equals the first-survey snow depth * first-survey snow density.
      #The total ice melt is the total melt depth less the first-survey snow depth * ice density
      #If there is still snow around the stake at the last survey, then the melt is all snow, but the amount is complicated as snow can compress over summer.
      #The total snow melt is the (first-survey snow depth * first-survey snow density) minus (last-survey snow depth * last-survey snow density)

  if (TotalSurfaceLowering[StakeIndex] > InitialSnowDepth * 1000){

    SnowMeltSWE <- SnowDepthToSWE(InitialSnowDepth*1000, min(SurveyDates),PitData = PitData)
    IceMeltSWE <- (TotalSurfaceLowering[StakeIndex] - InitialSnowDepth*1000)/1000 * IceDensity
    TotalSWEMelt[StakeIndex] <- SnowMeltSWE + IceMeltSWE
  } else {
    TotalSWEMelt[StakeIndex] <- SnowDepthToSWE(InitialSnowDepth*1000, min(SurveyDates),PitData = PitData) - 
      SnowDepthToSWE(FinalSnowDepth * 1000, max(SurveyDates),PitData=PitData)
  }
  
}

#The TotalSWEMelt needs to be added to the stake spatial data as an attribute
#Get the locations of the stakes of the first survey
InitialStakeLocations <- spStakePoints[spStakePoints$Date == min(SurveyDates),]
InitialStakeLocations$TotalSWEMelt <- TotalSWEMelt
InitialStakeLocations$TotalMeltDepth <- TotalSurfaceLowering
```
The melt over the whole ablation part of the glacier needs to be interpolated from the stake measurements. This is done by assuming the primary control on melt is elevation, and using the glacier elevation to distribute the melt observations. In addition to the stake measurements, the end-of-summer-snowline has been used to provide an additional elevation-to-snow melt point.

The average elevation of the EOSS is required and the average winter SWE at that elevation.
Use the elevation-area hypsometric curve and the accumulation area for the glacier to determine the EOSS elevation.

A relationship between melt and elevation is determined (including the stakes and the EOSS elevation, EOSS winter SWE), applied to the DEM and spatially clipped to the ablation area.
The total melt is then calculated.
```{r}
#Get the elevation of the stakes by sampling the DEM at the stake locations
StakeDEMElevations <- terra::extract(RollestonDEM,spStakePoints,ID=FALSE)[FirstStakeIndices,]

# Normalise column name for backwards compatibility - these are different between years in the input data
area_type_col <- if ("Type" %in% names(AccumulationAblationAreas)) "Type" else "AreaType"

#Get the elevation of the EOSS. This is done by finding the area of the end-of-summer ablation area, and then reading off the elevation from the area-elevation hypsometric curve created earlier.
#Note that this is an approximation to get around the problem of the EOSS not really being at a single elevation.
#AblationArea <- gArea(AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas$Type=="Ablation",])
AblationArea <- terra::expanse(AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas$Type=="Ablation",])
AccumulationArea <- terra::expanse(AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas$Type=="Accumulation",])
EOSSElevation <- AreaElevationCurve[which.min(abs(AreaElevationCurve$Area-AblationArea)),'Elevation']

#Get the end-of-winter snow depth (in swe) for the EOSS line
EOSSMelt <- mean(terra::extract(EOWSWERaster,EOSSLine,ID=FALSE)[,1],na.rm=TRUE)

#Create a linear model relating melt to elevation, including the EOSS melt and elevation
MeltElevationModel <- lm(melt ~ elevation, list(melt = c(TotalSWEMelt,EOSSMelt),elevation = c(StakeDEMElevations,EOSSElevation)))

#Use that model to apply to the elevation raster
MeltRaster <- MeltElevationModel$coefficients[2]* GlacierDEM + MeltElevationModel$coefficients[1]

#Restrict to the ablation area
AblationMelt <- terra::mask(MeltRaster,AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas$Type=="Ablation",])

#Calculate average melt over the ablation area
paste0("Area averaged summer melt over the ablation area of ",round(mean(AblationMelt[!is.na(AblationMelt)]),0), " mm of snow water equivalent")
```

Plot the ablation area summer melt
```{r}
{
plot(AblationMelt, main = "Ablation Area Summer Melt")
plot(AccumulationAblationAreas,add=T)
}
```
Estimate uncertainty for ablation area. This is going to be the dominant uncertainty in the mass balance calculation because we are extraplotating a linear trend from very few points across the ablation area.
```{r}
# Get the elevation from every cell in the DEM into a dataframe so it can be fed into predict()
DEM_df <- data.frame(elevation = terra::values(GlacierDEM, na.rm = FALSE))
names(DEM_df) <- "elevation"

# Feed every elevation through the melt elevation linear model and get standard error of the predicted mean melt for every elevation
Predictions <- predict(MeltElevationModel, newdata = DEM_df, se.fit = TRUE)

# Build standard error raster matching the DEM grid, mask to the ablation area
MeltSERaster <- GlacierDEM
terra::values(MeltSERaster) <- Predictions$se.fit
AblationMeltSE <- terra::mask(MeltSERaster, AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas[[area_type_col]] == "Ablation",])

# Combine the per-pixel standard error values into one ablation area uncertainty 
sigma_Bs_ablation_regression <- sqrt(mean(AblationMeltSE[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))

# Pixel-level uncertainty (mm w.e.) from assumption of uniform density profile:

# Get initial winter SWE at each pixel, masked to ablation area. Then split predicted melt into snow-derived and ice-derived components
EOWSWERaster_resampled <- terra::resample(EOWSWERaster, GlacierDEM, method = "bilinear") # need to resample EOWSWERaster onto same grid as AblationMelt
InitialSWE_raster <- terra::mask(EOWSWERaster_resampled, AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas[[area_type_col]] == "Ablation",]) #Mask to ablation area
MeltFromSnowSWE <- min(AblationMelt, InitialSWE_raster) # how much melted, capped at how much snow there was
MeltFromIceSWE  <- max(AblationMelt - InitialSWE_raster, 0) # whatever is leftover after snow melt is ice

# Get EOS pit by filtering on survey month, then get the LUT and extract average density at maximum pit depth. 
EOSPitData <- PitData[[which(sapply(PitData, function(x) {
  as.integer(format(as.Date(x[1, 3], format = "%d/%m/%Y"), "%m")) %in% 2:4 # February to April for EOS pit
}))]]
EOSPitLUT  <- DepthToDensityLUT(EOSPitData)
EOSMaxDepth <- max(EOSPitData[, 8], na.rm = TRUE)
EOS_density_mean <- EOSPitLUT$AveDensity[EOSPitLUT$Depth == EOSMaxDepth]

# Snow/firn density uncertainty, ice density uncertainty assumed negligible (SD = 0)
sigma_snow_density_raster <- (MeltFromSnowSWE / EOS_density_mean) * EOS_density_sd_all
sigma_ice_density_raster <- (MeltFromIceSWE / IceDensity) * 0

# Combined density uncertainty raster
sigma_Bs_ablation_density_raster <- sqrt(sigma_snow_density_raster^2 + sigma_ice_density_raster^2)

# Pixel-level combined uncertainty (mm w.e.) from density and regression
# AblationMeltSE is a standard error (from predict se.fit), not variance, so square it first
sigma_Bs_ablation_combined <- sqrt(AblationMeltSE^2 + sigma_Bs_ablation_density_raster^2)

# Ablation area combined uncertainty
sigma_Bs_ablation_density <- sqrt(mean(sigma_Bs_ablation_density_raster[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))
sigma_Bs_ablation_total   <- sqrt(mean(sigma_Bs_ablation_combined[]^2,       na.rm = TRUE))

paste0("σ regression: ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bs_ablation_regression), " mm w.e.")
paste0("σ density: ",    sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bs_ablation_density),    " mm w.e.")
paste0("σ total (combined): ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bs_ablation_total), " mm w.e.")

# Uncertainty contributions
var_regression_Bs <- mean(AblationMeltSE[]^2,                       na.rm = TRUE)
var_density_Bs     <- mean(sigma_Bs_ablation_density_raster[]^2,     na.rm = TRUE)
total_var_Bs        <- var_regression_Bs + var_density_Bs

paste0(sprintf("Regression uncertainty contribution: %.1f%%", 100 * var_regression_Bs/total_var_Bs))
paste0(sprintf("Density uncertainty contribution:    %.1f%%", 100 * var_density_Bs/total_var_Bs))

# Plot combined uncertainty
{
plot(sigma_Bs_ablation_combined,
     main = "Combined EOS Melt Uncertainty - Ablation Area (mm w.e.)",
     col  = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
     legend = TRUE)
plot(RollestonGlacierOutline, add = TRUE)
plot(AccumulationAblationAreas, add = TRUE)
plot(spStakePoints[FirstStakeIndices, ], add = TRUE)
}

```


# End of Summer accumulation area interpolation
The summer snow interpolation should include zero values on the edge of the accumulation area that is not on the edge of the glacier.
Interpolate the end-of-summer snow depth observations in a similar manner to the end-of-winter ones, except include the EOSS values as 0. This requires use of the end-of-summer-snowline.
Once completed, subtract the end-of-summer values from the end-of-winter values to find the total melt over summer. Clip this to the accumulation area. Combine this with the ablation area data to get the total summer melt.

In 2025, only one line of snow depths were made, with the assumption that the depth profile was similar near the headwall along the glacier. For this assumption to be included in the snow depth interpolation, a snow depth "virtual" file was created. This created "virtual" snow depths based on expert opinion of what the snow depth was likely to have been. These data need to be used for the snow depth interpolation.

Create a flag for years with no summer probe data because of no remaining snow
```{r}
# 2018 has no probe data. Check before doing anything else.
eos_no_data <- is.null(spProbePoints[["EndOfSummer"]])

if (eos_no_data) {
  EOSSWERaster5mGlacier <- terra::mask(
    GlacierDEM - GlacierDEM,
    AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas[[area_type_col]] == "Accumulation", ]
  )
  message("No end-of-summer probe data — accumulation area set to zero SWE. Skip kriging chunks.")
}
```

Prepare data for kriging
```{r}
#reminder to not try to calculate end of summer snow if there were no snow depth measurements at the end of summer
if (eos_no_data) stop("No data year — do not run this chunk.")

#Sample along the End-Of-Summer-Snowline at 20 m interval and make these zero values
EOSSSampleSize <- floor(terra::perim(EOSSLine)/20)

EOSSSample <- sf::st_as_sf(EOSSLine) %>%
  st_cast(to="LINESTRING",warn=FALSE) %>%
  st_line_sample(n = EOSSSampleSize, type = "regular") %>%
  terra::vect() %>%
  terra::disagg()
EOSSSample$SWE <- 0

#Get the end of summer snow depths
EndOfSummerDepths <- spProbePoints[["EndOfSummer"]]

#Get the end of summer virtual snow depths (if they exist)
if ("EndOfSummer_Virtual" %in% names(ProbeData)){
  VirtualSummerDepths <- spProbePoints[["EndOfSummer_Virtual"]]
  EndOfSummerDepths <- rbind(EndOfSummerDepths,VirtualSummerDepths) %>%
    terra::unique()
}

#Some years there is no end-of-summer probes because there is not much snow (e.g. 2018), so only interpolate if they exist
if (!is.null(EndOfSummerDepths)){
  #Convert depths to snow water equivalent using the pit density data
  EndOfSummerDepths$SWE <- SnowDepthToSWE(EndOfSummerDepths$Snow_Depth_m*1000, max(ProbedDates),PitData = PitData)
  
  #Combine the EOSS points (set to 0), with the snow depth observations
  EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS <- terra::union(EOSSSample,EndOfSummerDepths)
  #EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS <- EndOfSummerDepths
  
  #Need to get rid of any duplicate locations
  EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS <- terra::unique(EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS)
  
  #Add DEM values to EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS
  EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS$DEMValues <- terra::extract(
    RollestonDEM, EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS, ID = FALSE)
  
  # Turn into an sf object for kriging and get rid of NA values
  eos_depths_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS)
  eos_depths_sf <- eos_depths_sf[!is.na(eos_depths_sf$SWE) & !is.na(eos_depths_sf$DEMValues), ]
}
```

Estimate spatial trend and normality to see if ordinary or universal kriging is appropriate. If there is no skew and there isn't a trend in SWE with elevation, use ordinary kriging.
```{r}
if (!is.null(EndOfSummerDepths)){
  
  #Check for skew
  hist(EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS$SWE)
  
  # check if there is a trend in SWE with elevation
  plot(eos_depths_sf$DEMValues, eos_depths_sf$SWE,
       xlab = "Elevation (m)",
       ylab = "SWE (mm)")
  abline(lm(SWE ~ DEMValues, data = eos_depths_sf))
  
  #fit a trend model, plot the histogram of the residuals
  elev_mod <- lm(SWE ~ DEMValues, data = eos_depths_sf)
  eos_depths_sf$resid <- residuals(elev_mod)
  hist(eos_depths_sf$resid)
}
```

Plot sample/experimental variograms - one ordinary, and one with the residuals after removing elevation trend. The variance explained by the elevation trend is the difference between the two curves. If the curves are the same, can use ordinary kriging.
```{r}
if (!is.null(EndOfSummerDepths)){
  
  #Cutoff heuristic - same as EOW
  coords <- terra::crds(EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS)
  dists <- dist(coords)
  max_dist <- max(dists)
  cutoff <- max_dist / 2
  
  #generate experimental/sample variogram from residuals after removing elevation trend. 
  SampleVariogram <- variogram(SWE ~ DEMValues,eos_depths_sf, cutoff = cutoff) 
  
  #compare residual variogram to variogram plotted from the data 
  SampleVariogram_ordinary <- variogram(SWE ~ 1, eos_depths_sf, cutoff = cutoff)
  
  #Plot on one graph
  # Set axis limits
  xlim <- range(c(SampleVariogram$dist,SampleVariogram_ordinary$dist))
  ylim <- range(c(SampleVariogram$gamma,SampleVariogram_ordinary$gamma))
  
  # Create plot
  plot(SampleVariogram$dist,
       SampleVariogram$gamma,
       col = "blue",
       xlim = xlim,
       ylim = ylim,
       xlab = "Distance",
       ylab = "Semivariance",
       main="Sample Variograms EOS")
  
  # Add second variogram
  points(SampleVariogram_ordinary$dist,
         SampleVariogram_ordinary$gamma,
         col = "red")
  
  legend("topleft",
         legend = c("Residuals", "Ordinary"),
         col = c("blue", "red"),
         pch = c(1, 1))
}
```

Plot variograms for comparison and krige using ordinary kriging - can change this if there is a trend in SWE with elevation
```{r}
if (is.null(EndOfSummerDepths)) stop("No data year — do not run this chunk.")
  
  #fitting different models to compare. gaussian unlikely to be any good?
  #fit.variogram only optimises sill/range/nugget, anisotropy values are fixed.
  sph.fit <- fit.variogram(
    SampleVariogram_ordinary,
    vgm(psill=psill.start, "Sph", range=range.start, nugget=nugget.start),
    fit.method=7
  )
  
  exp.fit <- fit.variogram(
    SampleVariogram_ordinary,
    vgm(psill=psill.start, "Exp", range=range.start, nugget=nugget.start),
    fit.method=7
  )
  
  gau.fit <- fit.variogram(
    SampleVariogram_ordinary,
    vgm(psill=psill.start, "Gau", range=range.start, nugget=nugget.start),
    fit.method=7
  )
  
  #plot to visually compare
  plot(SampleVariogram_ordinary, sph.fit, main="sph")
  plot(SampleVariogram_ordinary, exp.fit, main="exp")
  plot(SampleVariogram_ordinary, gau.fit, main="gau")
  
  # Collect the SSErr values, pick the best (lowest weighted residual sum of squares)
  sserr <- c(Sph=attr(sph.fit, "SSErr"), Exp=attr(exp.fit, "SSErr"), Gau=attr(gau.fit, "SSErr"))
  best_model_name <- names(which.min(sserr))
  message("Auto-selected model: ", best_model_name)
  vari.model <- list(Sph=sph.fit, Exp=exp.fit, Gau=gau.fit)[[best_model_name]]
  
  #Ordinary kriging. Using 12 points at a time. Spatial data needs to be an sf object. 
  #Point kriging onto the grid, predicts SWE and variance at each cell
  KrigedEOSSWE <- krige(
    #SWE ~ DEMValues, # Universal kriging, change to this if there is a trend in SWE with elevation
    SWE ~ 1, # Ordinary kriging
    locations = eos_depths_sf,
    newdata   = sf::st_as_sf(GlacierGrid),
    model     = vari.model,
    nmax      = 12
  )

```

Plot accumulation area results
```{r}

#If there were any non-zero accumulation measurements, krig them
if (!is.null(EndOfSummerDepths)){
  #prepare raster for plotting kriged results
#Note the need to adjust the extent to be 60 m greater than the kriged points, as the kriged points were prepared using the GlacierGrid centres
  r <- (terra::ext(RollestonGlacierOutline) + 60) %>%
    terra::rast(resolution = 30, crs = terra::crs(RollestonGlacierOutline))
  
#Convert the kriged points to spatial point data, with the projection matching the Rolleston outline  
  KrigedEOSSWE_v <- terra::vect(KrigedEOSSWE)
  KrigedEOSSWE_v <- terra::project(KrigedEOSSWE_v, terra::crs(RollestonGlacierOutline))
  
  #Convert the points to a raster
  EOSSWERaster   <- terra::rasterize(KrigedEOSSWE_v, r, field = 'var1.pred')
  
  #Resample to 5 m and align with the DEM grid  
  EOSSWERaster5m<- terra::resample(EOSSWERaster, RollestonDEM)
  
  #Restrict to the accumulation area
  EOSSWERaster5mGlacier <- terra::mask(
    EOSSWERaster5m,
    AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas[[area_type_col]] == "Accumulation", ]
    )

} else {
  EOSSWERaster5mGlacier <- terr::mask(GlacierDEM - GlacierDEM,AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas$Type=="Accumulation",])
}

#Subtract the summer remaining snow from the end-of-winter snow
AccumulationAreaMelt <- EOWSWERaster5mGlacier- EOSSWERaster5mGlacier

#Calculate average melt over the accumulation area
paste0("Area averaged summer melt over the accumulation area of ",round(mean(AccumulationAreaMelt[!is.na(AccumulationAreaMelt)]),0), " mm of snow water equivalent")

paste0("Area averaged annual gain over the accumulation area of ",round(mean(EOSSWERaster5mGlacier[!is.na(AccumulationAreaMelt)]),0), " mm of snow water equivalent")

paste("Accumulation area size:",round(AccumulationArea/1000000,3),"km2" )

paste("Area of ablation area that would lead to a balanced glacier (km2):")
mean(EOSSWERaster5mGlacier[!is.na(AccumulationAreaMelt)]) * AccumulationArea / mean(AblationMelt[!is.na(AblationMelt)]) /1000000
paste("Ablation area size this year:",round(AblationArea/1000000,3),"km2")
```

```{r}
plot(AccumulationAblationAreas,add=T)
}
```

Assess kriging results using leave one out cross validation, same as EOW
```{r}
#leave out out cross validation (cv)
cv <- krige.cv(SWE~1,locations=eos_depths_sf,model=vari.model,nmax=12,debug.level=0)

#plot cv results. dashed line is 1:1 line
cv_df <- data.frame(
  observed = cv$observed,
  predicted = cv$var1.pred
)
ggplot(cv_df, aes(x = observed, y = predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_equal() +
  xlab("Observed SWE") +
  ylab("Predicted SWE")+ggtitle("Cross validation results EOS")
```

Uncertainty calculations for accumulation area - same process as EOW
```{r}
# Kriging error calculations
ME <- mean(cv$residual)
RMSE <- sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2))
MSDR <- mean((cv$residual^2) / cv$var1.var)

paste0("Mean error: ", sprintf("%.2f", ME), " (mm w.e.)") 
paste0("Root mean squared error: ", sprintf("%.2f", RMSE), " (mm w.e.)") 
paste0("Mean squared deviation ratio: ", sprintf("%.2f", MSDR)) 

# Kriging variance raster - masked to the accumulation area
EOSSWEVarRaster <- terra::rasterize(KrigedEOSSWE_v, r, field = 'var1.var')
EOSSWEVarRaster5m <- terra::resample(EOSSWEVarRaster, RollestonDEM)
AccumulationAreaPolygon <- AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas[[area_type_col]] == "Accumulation", ]
EOSSWEVarRaster5mAccum <- terra::mask(EOSSWEVarRaster5m, AccumulationAreaPolygon)

# Convert prediction variance (mm2 w.e.) to kriging standard error (mm w.e., same as SWE) for plotting
EOSSWESERaster5mAccum   <- sqrt(EOSSWEVarRaster5mAccum)

# Calculate glacier-wide kriging uncertainty
sigma_EOS_krig    <- sqrt(mean(EOSSWEVarRaster5mAccum[], na.rm = TRUE))

# Plot kriging standard error with probe and EOSS point locations
{
plot(EOSSWESERaster5mAccum,
     main = "EOS Accumlation Area Kriging Standard Error (mm w.e.)",
     col  = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
     legend = TRUE)
plot(RollestonGlacierOutline, add = T)
plot(EndOfSummerDepthsAndEOSS, add=T)
plot(AccumulationAblationAreas,add=T)
}

# Root mean square (RMS) kriging standard error over the accumulation area 
sigma_EOS_krig    <- sqrt(mean(EOSSWEVarRaster5mAccum[], na.rm = TRUE))

# Pixel-level uncertainty (mm we) from assumption of uniform density profile
sigma_Bs_density_raster <- (EOSSWERaster5mGlacier / EOS_density_mean) * EOS_density_sd_all

# Pixel level uncertainty combined (mm w.e.)
sigma_Bs_combined <- sqrt(EOSSWEVarRaster5mAccum + sigma_Bs_density_raster^2)

# Accumulation area combined uncertainty 
sigma_Bs_density <- sqrt(mean(sigma_Bs_density_raster[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))
sigma_Bs_total <- sqrt(mean(sigma_Bs_combined[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))

paste0("σ kriging: ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_EOS_krig), " mm w.e.")
paste0("σ density: ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bs_density), " mm w.e.")
paste0("σ total (combined): ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Bs_total), " mm w.e.")

# Uncertainty contributions
var_krig_Bs    <- mean(EOSSWEVarRaster5mAccum[],      na.rm = TRUE)
var_density_Bs <- mean(sigma_Bs_density_raster[]^2,     na.rm = TRUE)
total_var_Bs   <- var_krig_Bs + var_density_Bs

paste0(sprintf("Kriging uncertainty contribution:  %.1f%%", 100 * var_krig_Bs/total_var_Bs))
paste0(sprintf("Density uncertainty contribution:  %.1f%%", 100 * var_density_Bs/total_var_Bs))

```

```{r}
paste0("Annual Mass Balance-",MassBalanceYear-1,"-",MassBalanceYear,".tif")),overwrite=TRUE)

```

```{r}
#Plot annual balance
# Symmetric colour limits centred on zero

breaks <- seq(-abs_max, abs_max, length.out = 101)

plot(AnnualBalance, 
     main = paste("Mass balance (mm),", MassBalanceYear - 1, "-", MassBalanceYear), 
     col = rev(hcl.colors(100, "Blue-Red 3")),
     breaks = breaks,
     type = "continuous")
plot(RollestonGlacierOutline, add = T)
plot(EOSSLine, add = T)

```
Annual balance uncertainty
```{r}
# Annual balance uncertainty raster - quadrature sum of winter and summer at each pixel
AnnualBalanceUncertainty <- sqrt(sigma_bw_combined^2 + SummerUncertainty^2)

# Glacier-wide annual uncertainty - interpolation only - area is applied later
sigma_Ba_interp <- sqrt(mean(AnnualBalanceUncertainty[]^2, na.rm = TRUE))

# Glacier area/outline uncertainty, applied once at the glacier-wide level (Paul et al., 2013)
sigma_Ba_area <- MeanAnnualBalance * rel_sigma_area

# Combine interpolation and area uncertainty
sigma_Ba <- sqrt(sigma_Ba_interp^2 + sigma_Ba_area^2)

paste0("Area averaged mass balance change of ", MeanAnnualBalance, 
       " ± ", sprintf("%.0f", sigma_Ba), " mm of snow water equivalent")

{
plot(AnnualBalanceUncertainty,
     main = "Combined Annual Balance Uncertainty (mm w.e.)",
     col  = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
     legend = TRUE)
plot(RollestonGlacierOutline, add = TRUE)
plot(EOSSLine, add = T)
}
```

So I now have stake melt, snow depths, winter balance, summer balance and annual balance.
I should spit out the numbers in a table ready for WGMS.
I need to know the maximum and minimum number of measurements in the accmulaton area and the ablation area (see WGMS submission guidleines)

```{r}
#Create a dataframe of the useful stuff
BalanceTotals <- data.frame(WinterBalance = WinterAccumulation,
           SummerBalance = SummerMelt,
             AnnualBalance = MeanAnnualBalance)

BalanceTotals
paste("Equilibrium line altitude = ",round(EOSSElevation),"m asl")

#Find the number of measurements in the summer and winter in the accumulation and ablation areas. Assume the stakes last the whole year.
spWinterPit <- terra::vect( unique(PitData[[1]][,c("Easting.NZTM.","Northing.NZTM.")]),geom=c("Easting.NZTM.","Northing.NZTM."),crs='epsg:2193')
#In the case where no summer pit was dug (e.g. 2018) just set the location completely off grid!
if(length(PitData) > 1){
spSummerPit <- terra::vect( unique(PitData[[2]][,c("Easting.NZTM.","Northing.NZTM.")]),geom=c("Easting.NZTM.","Northing.NZTM."),crs='epsg:2193')
} else spSummerPit <- terra::vect(data.frame('Easting.NZTM.' = 0,'Northing.NZTM.'=0),geom=c("Easting.NZTM.","Northing.NZTM."),crs='epsg:2193')

#Winter accumulation area observation count
PitsAccumulation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Accumulation") %>% terra::relate(spWinterPit,relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
StakesAccumulation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Accumulation") %>% terra::relate(spStakePoints[spStakePoints$Date == SurveyDates[1],],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
ProbesAccumulation1 <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Accumulation") %>% terra::relate(spProbePoints[[1]],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
TotalWinterObsInAccumulationArea <- PitsAccumulation + StakesAccumulation + ProbesAccumulation1

#Summer accumulation area observation count
PitsAccumulation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Accumulation") %>% terra::relate(spSummerPit,relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
StakesAccumulation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Accumulation") %>% terra::relate(spStakePoints[spStakePoints$Date == tail(SurveyDates,1),],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()

#In the case where no summer probes were made (e.g. 2018) just set the probe locations to 0
if(length(spProbePoints)>1){
ProbesAccumulation2 <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Accumulation") %>% terra::relate(spProbePoints[[2]],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()

} else ProbesAccumulation2 <- 0
TotalSummerObsInAccumulationArea <- PitsAccumulation + StakesAccumulation + ProbesAccumulation2

MIN_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ACCUMULATION_AREA <- min(TotalWinterObsInAccumulationArea ,TotalSummerObsInAccumulationArea)
MAX_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ACCUMULATION_AREA <- max(TotalWinterObsInAccumulationArea ,TotalSummerObsInAccumulationArea)

#Winter ablation area observation count
PitsAblation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Ablation") %>% terra::relate(spWinterPit,relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
StakesAblation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Ablation") %>% terra::relate(spStakePoints[spStakePoints$Date == SurveyDates[1],],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
ProbesAblation1 <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Ablation") %>% terra::relate(spProbePoints[[1]],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()

TotalWinterObsInAblationArea <- PitsAblation + StakesAblation + ProbesAblation1

#Summer ablation area observation count
PitsAblation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Ablation") %>% terra::relate(spSummerPit,relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
StakesAblation <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Ablation") %>% terra::relate(spStakePoints[spStakePoints$Date == tail(SurveyDates,1),],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow()
#In the case where no summer probes were made (e.g. 2018) just set the probe locations to 0
if(length(spProbePoints) >1) ProbesAblation2 <- AccumulationAblationAreas %>% terra::subset(.$Type == "Ablation") %>% terra::relate(spProbePoints[[2]],relation= "contains", pairs=TRUE) %>% nrow() else ProbesAblation2 <- 0

TotalSummerObsInAblationArea <- PitsAblation + StakesAblation + ProbesAblation2

MIN_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ABLATION_AREA <- min(TotalWinterObsInAblationArea ,TotalSummerObsInAblationArea)
MAX_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ABLATION_AREA <- max(TotalWinterObsInAblationArea ,TotalSummerObsInAblationArea)

#AccumulationArea <- terra::expanse(AccumulationAblationAreas[AccumulationAblationAreas$Type=="Accumulation",])

paste("MinObsInAcc:",MIN_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ACCUMULATION_AREA)
paste("MaxObsInAcc:",MAX_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ACCUMULATION_AREA)
paste("MinObsInAbl:",MIN_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ABLATION_AREA)
paste("MaxObsInAbl:",MAX_NUMBER_OF_MEASUREMENT_SITES_IN_ABLATION_AREA)
paste("Accumulation area size:",round(AccumulationArea/1000000,3),"km2" )
paste("Ablation area size:",round(AblationArea/1000000,3),"km2" )
paste("Accumulation area ratio:", round(AccumulationArea / (AblationArea + AccumulationArea) * 100), "%")
paste("Glacier area (m2):",round((AblationArea + AccumulationArea)), "m2")
```
For the WGMS Submission form I need a table of information describing the point measurements. This is all the probe and stake observations.
For each one I need to know the date range for which the measurements apply, any identification of the observation, location, in lat lon, and elevation (m asl), the point balance in m we, the density used (in kg / m3) for depth to water equivalent conversions, the "balance code", either BW for winter balance, or BS for summer balance or BA for Annual balance. Winter pobing is BW, stakes are BS, summer probes are BA. Summer probe start times are from the previous summer probe date. 
```{r}
#Start with winter balances. These are the probed depths.
EndOfWinterDepths[,c("Longitude","Latitude")] <- terra::project(EndOfWinterDepths,'epsg:4326') %>% terra::crds(df=TRUE)
EndOfWinterDepths$Density <-  round(EndOfWinterDepths$SWE / EndOfWinterDepths$Snow_Depth_m)
EndOfWinterDepths$WGMSBalanceCode <- "BW"
View(as.data.frame(EndOfWinterDepths)[,c("Latitude","Longitude","DEMValues","SWE","Density")])

#Summer balances are the stake observations
InitialStakeLocations[,c("Longitude","Latitude")] <- terra::project(InitialStakeLocations,'epsg:4326') %>% terra::crds(df=TRUE) 
InitialStakeLocations$DEMValues <- terra::extract(RollestonDEM, InitialStakeLocations,ID=FALSE)
InitialStakeLocations$Density <-round(InitialStakeLocations$TotalSWEMelt /
                                           InitialStakeLocations$TotalMeltDepth * 1000)
InitialStakeLocations$WGMSBalanceCode <- "BS"
InitialStakeLocations$SWE <- InitialStakeLocations$TotalSWEMelt
InitialStakeLocations$Point_ID <- paste0("Stake",order(InitialStakeLocations$Elevation..mae.,decreasing = TRUE))
View(as.data.frame(InitialStakeLocations)[,c("Point_ID","Latitude","Longitude","DEMValues","TotalSWEMelt","Density")])

#And any summer probes
EndOfSummerDepths[,c("Longitude","Latitude")] <- terra::project(EndOfSummerDepths,'epsg:4326') %>% terra::crds(df=TRUE)  
EndOfSummerDepths$Density <-  round(EndOfSummerDepths$SWE / EndOfSummerDepths$Snow_Depth_m)
EndOfSummerDepths$DEMValues <- terra::extract(RollestonDEM, EndOfSummerDepths,ID=FALSE)
EndOfSummerDepths$WGMSBalanceCode <- "BA"
View(as.data.frame(EndOfSummerDepths)[,c("Latitude","Longitude","DEMValues","SWE","Density")])

#Combine the three tables and save as a csv file for easy copying into the WGMS form
#### need to still add ID, from and to dates and uncertainties.*****
PointBalanceData <- rbind(EndOfWinterDepths[c("Point_ID","Latitude","Longitude","DEMValues","SWE","Density","WGMSBalanceCode")],
                          InitialStakeLocations[c("Point_ID","Latitude","Longitude","DEMValues","SWE","Density","WGMSBalanceCode")],
                          EndOfSummerDepths[c("Point_ID","Latitude","Longitude","DEMValues","SWE","Density","WGMSBalanceCode")])

#remove any 0 SummerDepth values, as these have an unknown balance.
PointBalanceData <- PointBalanceData[!((PointBalanceData$SWE == 0) & (PointBalanceData$WGMSBalanceCode == "BA")),]

write.csv(PointBalanceData,file.path(CurrentYearDataDirectory,"MassBalancePointDataForWGMSSubmission.csv") )
```



For bonus points the WGMS like elevation-banded mass balances areas.
This may be generated from a combination of the DEM and the Annual mass balance maps
I have arbitrarily selected 20 m elevation bands
```{r}
#From the DEM bin all the elevations into equal sized bins
BinLowElevations <- seq(from = 1720,to= 1900, by = 20)
BinHighElevations <- BinLowElevations + 20
#DEMBins <- split(DEMData, findInterval(DEMData,BinLowElevations))

#Calculate the area in each bin (same as the number of cells multiplied by the resolution) and the average elevation of each bin
#BinAreas <- sapply(DEMBins, function(x) {length(x) * prod(res(GlacierDEM))})

#BinAreaPct <- round(BinAreas * 100 / sum(BinAreas))

#Build the look up table of elevation vs total area
#ElevationHypsography <- data.frame(ElevationLow = BinLowElevations, ElevationHigh = BinHighElevations, AreaPct = BinAreaPct)

#For the mass balance I need to get the average mass balance for each elevation band.
#Start by creating a raster with each elevation band.
#Reclasify the glacier DEM into elevation bands
ReclassMatrix <- cbind(BinLowElevations,BinHighElevations,seq(1,length(BinLowElevations)))
ElevationBands <- terra::classify(GlacierDEM, ReclassMatrix)

CellsInEachBand <- terra::zonal(GlacierDEM/GlacierDEM, ElevationBands, fun='sum')
BandAreaPct     <- round(CellsInEachBand[,2] / sum(CellsInEachBand[,2]) * 100)
MassBalancePerBand <- terra::zonal(AnnualBalance, ElevationBands, fun='mean') %>% round()

ElevationBandData <- data.frame(ElevationLow = BinLowElevations, ElevationHigh = BinHighElevations, AreaPct = BandAreaPct,MassBalance_mm=MassBalancePerBand[,2])
write.table(ElevationBandData,file.path(DataDirectory,"IndividualYears",paste0(MassBalanceYear-1,"-",MassBalanceYear),paste0("ElevationBandData",MassBalanceYear,".csv")),quote = FALSE,sep=",",row.names = FALSE)

```
